guide_enrichment.narrative:
Our slight preference for Maryland starts with the stability we see in its passing game. Malik Washington has completed 53 of 72 passes for 533 yards without an interception through two games, while Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding and Chris Durr Jr. each topped 100 receiving yards at UConn. We are not treating that performance as proof, but it gives us more confidence in Maryland's ability to sustain drives than the market appears to have priced.

We also see a favorable path for Maryland's defense when UCLA has to throw. UCLA's passing efficiency has been a clear weakness in our numbers, and Maryland has already generated 10 sacks through two games. The concern is that UCLA's rushing offense grades much better, while our longer-run ratings are less impressed by Maryland's run defense than its early results might suggest.

For us, that split explains both the modest disagreement and the pass. We can make a reasonable case for Maryland through quarterback play and pass-rush pressure, but UCLA's potential advantage on the ground keeps the matchup close enough that the available price does not create meaningful value.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching UCLA's rushing offense against Maryland's run defense. Maryland limited UConn to 67 rushing yards, but we do not want to overreact to one game when our broader matchup numbers identify UCLA's ground game as its more credible offensive path.

If Maryland can force UCLA into passing situations, we think its pressure can become a meaningful factor. If UCLA consistently stays ahead of schedule on the ground, that would attack the area where we have the most uncertainty about Maryland and help explain why our model stops short of a stronger position.

recent_game.fact: Maryland improved to 2-0 with a 38-14 road win over UConn on Sept. 12, 2026.
Maryland outgained UConn 475-223, recorded 27 first downs and held the ball for 35:31.
Maryland completed 35 of 42 passes for 350 yards and rushed 36 times for 125 yards against UConn without committing a turnover.
Maryland's defense held UConn to 67 rushing yards and 156 passing yards, recorded five sacks and forced one lost fumble.
Maryland produced second-quarter scoring drives of 92 and 91 yards against UConn, its first game with multiple 90-yard drives since 2018.

opponent_notes.fact: Maryland's schedule lists UCLA visiting SECU Stadium on Sept. 26, 2026, with kickoff at 1:30 p.m. Eastern on BTN.

quarterback.fact: Starting quarterback Malik Washington is 53-of-72 for 533 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions through Maryland's first two games of 2026.
Washington completed 34 of 41 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns against UConn, including a Maryland-record 18 consecutive completions.
Washington started all 12 games as a true freshman in 2025 and finished that season with 2,963 passing yards, 17 passing touchdowns and 303 rushing yards.
Transfer backup quarterback Cardell Williams completed 4 of 5 passes for 60 yards and a touchdown and rushed five times for 49 yards in the opener against Hampton.

offensive_personnel.fact: Maryland's offensive line against UConn consisted of left tackle Rahtrel Perry, left guard Amory Hills, center Michael Hershey, right guard Ryan Howerton and right tackle Isaiah Wright; that unit blocked for 475 total yards.
Rahtrel Perry has made 39 consecutive career starts, the most among Maryland's offensive players.

Transfer receivers Na'eem Abdul-Rahim Gladding and Chris Durr Jr. both exceeded 100 receiving yards at UConn: Gladding had eight catches for 130 yards and a touchdown, while Durr had 10 catches for 106 yards and a touchdown.
Gladding, an Old Dominion transfer, leads Maryland through two games with 14 receptions for 187 yards and two touchdowns.
